questions.question: Define perishability in tourism services.
questions.solution_html:
• Define perishability in tourism services. /[C01]
  • Ans: Perishability in tourism services means that tourism products such as hotel rooms,
  • airline seats, and tour services cannot be stored for future use. If they are not used at the
  • time of availability, the opportunity and revenue are lost.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is rural tourism? [2x5 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• What is rural tourism? /[CO6]
  • Ans: Rural tourism refers to tourism activities that take place in rural areas, offering visitors
  • an opportunity to experience village life, local culture, traditions, agriculture, and natural
  • surroundings.

questions.question: What is the significance of service quality in tourism?
questions.solution_html:
• What is the significance of service quality in tourism? / [CO1]
  • Ans: Service quality plays a vital role in the success of the tourism industry. High service
  • quality ensures customer satisfaction, which leads to repeat visits and positive word -of-
  • mouth promotion. Since tourism services are intangible, the tourist’s experienc e depends
  • largely on the behaviour, efficiency, and professionalism of service providers. Good service
  • quality helps build a positive destination image, enhances customer loyalty, and gives a
  • competitive advantage to tourism businesses. It also contri butes to the overall growth and
  • sustainability of the tourism sector.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss the significance of community participation in the success of Swadesh Darshan projects.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the significance of community participation in the success of Swadesh
  • Darshan projects. /[CO6]
  • Ans: Community participation is essential for the success of Swadesh Darshan projects as
  • it ensures sustainable and inclusive tourism development. Local communities help
  • preserve cultural heritage, traditions, and local knowledge. Their involvement creates
  • employment opportunities, improves livelihoods, and builds a sense of ownership toward
  • tourism assets. Active participation also helps in maintaining infrastructure, providing
  • authentic tourist experiences, and reducing conflicts between tourists and resi dents.
  • Overall, community participation ensures long -term success and sustainability of the
  • project.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a short note on any two architectural heritage sites in India and their historical importance.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a short note on any two architectural heritage sites in India and their historical
  • importance. /[C05]
  • Ans:
  • Taj Mahal, Agra:
  • The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
  • It is a symbol of love and showcases the finest Mughal architecture with intricate marble
  • work.
  • Qutub Minar, Delhi:
  • Qutub Minar was constructed during the Delhi Sultanate period. It reflects early Indo-Islamic
  • architecture and marks the beginning of Muslim rule in India.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the main objectives and components of the PRASHAD Scheme.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the main objectives and components of the PRASHAD Scheme. /[C06]
  • Ans:
  • Objectives of PRASHAD Scheme:
  • • To develop pilgrimage destinations in a planned and sustainable manner
  • • To enhance tourist experience at spiritual destinations
  • • To improve infrastructure and amenities for pilgrims
  • Components of PRASHAD Scheme:
  • • Development of roads, pathways, and transport facilities
  • • Provision of sanitation, drinking water, and accommodation
  • • Improvement of tourist information centers and safety facilities
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe how Ajanta and Ellora Caves represent Indian culture
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how Ajanta and Ellora Caves represent Indian culture. /[005]
  • Ans: Ajanta and Ellora Caves represent India’s rich cultural and religious heritage. Ajanta
  • Caves depict Buddhist themes through paintings and sculptures, reflecting ancient Indian
  • art and philosophy. Ellora Caves showcase Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain monuments,
  • symbolizing religious harmony and tolerance. Together, they demonstrate India’s artistic
  • excellence, spiritual diversity, and architectural skills of ancient times.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a note on yoga as a wellness product.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on yoga as a wellness product. /[C03]
  • Ans: Yoga is an important wellness tourism product of India that focuses on physical,
  • mental, and spiritual health. It includes practices such as asanas, pranayama, and
  • meditation. Yoga helps reduce stress, improve flexibility, and promote inner peace. Today,
  • yoga retreats and wellness centers attract both domestic and international tourists,
  • contributing significantly to India’s wellness tourism sector.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a short note on Varanasi as a spiritual destination [5x5 = 25]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a short note on Varanasi as a spiritual destination. /[C04]
  • Ans: Varanasi is one of the oldest living cities in the world and an important spiritual center
  • in India. Located on the banks of the River Ganga, it is considered sacred by Hindus. Pilgrims
  • visit Varanasi for rituals, temple worship, and spiritual liberation. The ghats, temples, and
  • religious ceremonies make Varanasi a major spiritual tourism destination.
  • [5x5=25]
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the role of Sufi shrines in India’s pilgrimage tourism. / [CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of Sufi shrines in India’s pilgrimage tourism. /[CO3, CO4
  • Ans: Sufi shrines play a significant role in India’s pilgrimage tourism by promoting spiritual
  • harmony and cultural unity. These shrines attract devotees from different religions, castes,
  • and regions. Sufi saints preached messages of love, peace, and tolerance, which continue
  • to influence society today. Major Sufi shrines are centers of religious festivals, music, and
  • rituals such as qawwali, enhancing cultural tourism. Pilgrimage to these shrines supports
  • local economies through tourism-related activities and strengthens India’s image as a land
  • of spiritual diversity.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss the role of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in the development and promotion of tourism in the country. [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in the development
  • and promotion of tourism in the country. /[C06]
  • Ans: The Ministry of Tourism plays a vital role in the development and promotion of tourism
  • in India. It formulates tourism policies and implements schemes such as Swadesh Darshan
  • and PRASHAD to improve infrastructure and destination development. The ministry
  • promotes India globally through campaigns like “Incredible India. ” It also supports skill
  • development, capacity building, and sustainable tourism practices. By coordinating with
  • state governments and private stakeholders, the ministry contributes to em ployment
  • generation, economic growth, and the overall development of the tourism sector.
  • [15x1=15]
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
